memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore him. When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God commanded him. Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. - Gen 21:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The baby is named Isaac - which means "he laughs." What a name to carry! Both Abraham and Sarah had laughed when God promised this child; theirs was the laughter of disbelief, of amazement, of a promise too big to take in (Gen 17:17; 18:12). And now God, with beautiful poetry, gives their laughter back to them transformed - as the very name of their joy.

There is such grace in this. God did not shame Abraham and Sarah for their doubting laughter. Instead, He redeemed it. The laughter of "this can't be true" became the laughter of "God has done it!" What had been a symbol of their weakness of faith became the name of their greatest joy.

This is how God so often works. He takes our doubts, our failures, our weaknesses - and He weaves them into stories of grace. The very thing that once expressed our unbelief can become, in His hands, a monument to His faithfulness.

Notice too Abraham's obedience: he circumcised Isaac "as God commanded him." Joy did not make him careless; it made him faithful. When God fulfils His promises, our response should be glad obedience. Whatever laughter of doubt you have carried, God is able to turn it into the laughter of joy. He specialises in transforming what we thought was impossible into cause for praise.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Has God ever turned your doubt or weakness into a story of His grace?
- Does the joy of God's blessings lead you to glad obedience?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You redeem even my doubting laughter and turn it into joy. Take my weaknesses and weave them into stories of Your grace. Let Your faithfulness fill my heart with glad obedience.
Amen.
